findings.message: The sitemap.xml table contains unfilled placeholder tokens that should never appear in a client-facing deliverable: [SITEMAP_URL_COUNT], [SITEMAP_LOC_ASSESSMENT], [SITEMAP_HAS_LASTMOD], [SITEMAP_LASTMOD_ASSESSMENT], [SITEMAP_HAS_CHANGEFREQ], [SITEMAP_CHANGEFREQ_ASSESSMENT], [SITEMAP_HAS_PRIORITY], [SITEMAP_PRIORITY_ASSESSMENT], and [SITEMAP_GRADE]. These are template slots that were never substituted with real audit data.
findings.context: ## Discovery Files → ### sitemap.xml table: '| `<loc>` URLs | [SITEMAP_URL_COUNT] entries | [SITEMAP_LOC_ASSESSMENT] |' … '**Sitemap grade:** [SITEMAP_GRADE]'

findings.message: Appendix B contains an unfilled placeholder '[N]' in the narrative ('We recorded every internal link found on every audited page: [N] links in total') and then reports zero counts for every link class, which contradicts the Priority 2 / Div Soup section that references real internal links and anchor structures. The '[N]' token is a leaked template slot.
findings.context: ## Appendix B: Link Inventory — 'We recorded every internal link found on every audited page: [N] links in total.' followed by a table showing 0 for every link class.

findings.message: The Security Headers narrative directly contradicts the table immediately above it. The table marks HSTS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, and X-Content-Type-Options all as 'Yes', but the following paragraph states '4 of the five standard security headers are absent across every audited response: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS'. One of these must be a fabricated or incorrectly generated data state; the client cannot act on both simultaneously.
findings.context: ## Security Headers — table rows show 'Yes' for HSTS, Content-Security-Policy, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, immediately followed by: '4 of the five standard security headers are absent across every audited response: Content-Security-Policy (CSP), X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security).'

findings.message: The Agent Reading Pipeline table labels the 'Truncation Risk' check as 'Fail' and states '6 page(s) exceed the 250 KB threshold', but the data column then reports 'Largest page: 231 KB. Threshold: 250 KB.' — 231 KB does not exceed 250 KB, so the fail verdict and the data are internally inconsistent. A number appears to have been generated or copied incorrectly.
findings.context: ## Agent Reading Pipeline — Truncation Risk row: 'Fail | 6/6 | 6 page(s) exceed the 250 KB threshold … Largest page: 231 KB. Threshold: 250 KB.'

findings.message: The Security Headers per-page table is completely empty (no rows, no data) and the coverage line reads '0 of 0 audited URLs carry all five headers' with all per-header tallies showing '0/0'. For a report auditing 6 pages, reporting 0 of 0 URLs is a data-generation failure that will be immediately apparent to the client.
findings.context: ## Security Headers — '**Coverage:** 0 of 0 audited URLs carry all five headers.' and the per-page breakdown table contains no data rows, with HTTPS: 0/0 | HSTS: 0/0 | CSP: 0/0 | X-Frame-Options: 0/0 | X-Content-Type-Options: 0/0.

findings.message: Priority 4 bullet 3 ('Add language metadata (hreflang where multilingual pages exist) to assist machines in routing content to the correct audience context') contains no data anchor from this audit — no page URL, no count of missing hreflang tags, no specific page where it is absent. The parenthetical 'where multilingual pages exist' is a generic hedge that could appear in any audit for any site. The surrounding priority block scores MSC at 49/100 but does not link hreflang absence to that score or name a specific page.
findings.context: Priority 4: Metadata Stack Completeness 49/100 — bullet: 'Add language metadata (hreflang where multilingual pages exist) to assist machines in routing content to the correct audience context. Without explicit language signals, machines may serve content to the wrong audience or reduce its ranking confidence in language-specific retrieval contexts.'

findings.message: 'leaves something to be desired' equivalent phrasing: 'machines currently see a much thinner version of the site than human visitors do' is an inverse-framing construction that implies a damaging baseline without neutrally stating a score. The scores themselves (Discovery 25/100, MX Level 1) already carry that message; the rhetorical amplification reads as editorialising rather than consultant prose.
findings.context: ## Executive Summary — '…search crawlers, LLMs, and other automated machines currently see a much thinner version of the site than human visitors do.'

findings.message: US English spelling 'optimization' appears in the 'Full Optimization' phase label of the Next Steps table. The report otherwise uses British/neutral forms throughout (e.g. 'optimisation' is used in the SEO scoring methodology). This is a mixed-register inconsistency.
findings.context: ## Next Steps → What's Next table — Phase label: 'Full Optimization | P1, P2, P3, P4, P5 (P1-P5) | Full machine readiness…'
